item.title: China's top diplomat meets Russian presidential aide, chairman of Maritime Board
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, meets with Russian presidential aide and chairman of the Maritime Board Nikolai Patrushev in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- China's top diplomat Wang Yi met with Russian presidential aide and chairman of the Maritime Board Nikolai Patrushev in Beijing on Monday.
Conveying President Xi Jinping's cordial greetings to President Putin, Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, said the close communication between the two heads of state led bilateral relations to a higher quality and a higher level.
Under the guidance of the two heads of state, the strategic mutual trust between China and Russia has become more solid, cooperation in various fields has become more resilient, and multilateral coordination has been tightened, said Wang.
Wang noted that China and Russia both shoulder important responsibilities in international maritime affairs and have broad prospects for cooperation, adding that China stands ready to work with Russia to enhance the alignment of maritime strategies between the two countries.
Wang expressed congratulations on the State Duma election in Russia last month, noting that the results fully demonstrated the common will of the Russian people.
Patrushev conveyed President Putin's sincere greetings to President Xi, adding that maintaining close exchanges between the two heads of state is the best guarantee for the development of bilateral relations.
Russia is willing to enhance cooperation with China in areas such as multilateral maritime governance, draw on China's useful experience in shipbuilding, logistics, maritime trade and other fields, and join hands with China to promote the building of a maritime community with a shared future, adding a new dimension to the comprehensive strategic coordination between Russia and China, said Patrushev.

item.title: Chinese premier meets Vietnam's National Assembly chairman
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Tran Thanh Man, chairman of the National Assembly of Vietnam, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Tran Thanh Man, chairman of the National Assembly of Vietnam, in Beijing on Monday.
Reflecting "camaraderie plus brotherhood," Li said China is willing to work with Vietnam to continue traditional friendship, enhance unity and mutual trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, better benefit the two peoples, and inject positive energy into promoting regional and global stability and prosperity.
Li said that China stands ready to enhance alignment of development strategies with the Vietnamese side, expand and optimize the economic and trade pie between the two countries, and continuously improve the quality and efficiency of cooperation in areas such as connectivity, artificial intelligence, clean energy and the digital economy.
He called on the two sides to deepen people-to-people exchanges and cooperation in medicine, education, youth and other fields, to cement the public opinion foundation for China-Vietnam friendship. In the face of the complex and volatile international situation, China is ready to enhance communication and collaboration with Vietnam under multilateral frameworks such as APEC, China-ASEAN and the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation to jointly address risks and challenges, he said.
Li also expressed the hope that the legislative bodies of the two countries will strongly support the bilateral practical cooperation and play a greater role in providing legal guarantees and promoting people-to-people bonds.
Tran Thanh Man said Vietnam extends its heartfelt congratulations on China's new and significant achievements in economic and social development, with its economic growth rate ranking among the top of the world's major economies and its breakthroughs in scientific and technological innovation leading the world.
Vietnam has always regarded China as a top priority and a strategic choice in its foreign relations, firmly adheres to the one-China policy, and will maintain close exchanges with China at all levels in accordance with the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and two countries, Tran Thanh Man added.
The National Assembly of Vietnam attaches great importance to and highly recognizes Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, and is willing to enhance exchanges of experience in governance with China, he noted.

item.title: Xi congratulates Madise on assuming Estonian presidency
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday extended congratulations to Ulle Madise on her assumption of office as president of Estonia.
Xi said that China and Estonia enjoy a traditional friendship and that bilateral relations have maintained steady development in recent years, with continued progress in exchanges and cooperation across various fields, bringing benefits to the two peoples.
Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Estonia relations and stands ready to work with President Madise to take the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries this year as an opportunity to enhance political mutual trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and continuously enrich the contemporary connotations of bilateral relations.

item.title: Xi, Papua New Guinea's governor-general exchange congratulations over 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Bob Dadae, governor-general of Papua New Guinea, on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
In his message, Xi noted that Papua New Guinea is a good friend, good partner and good brother of China in the Pacific island region.
Over the past 50 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in mutually beneficial cooperation, and expanded people-to-people exchanges, raising bilateral relations to new heights, Xi said. These achievements have benefited the two peoples and injected strong impetus into building a China-Pacific Island countries community with a shared future, said Xi.
Noting that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Papua New Guinea relations, Xi said that he stands ready to work with Dadae to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, strengthen exchanges and cooperation across various fields, and elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea to a new level, so as to deliver greater benefits to the two peoples.
For his part, Dadae said that over the past 50 years, bilateral relations have made significant progress, benefiting both countries and their peoples.
Papua New Guinea cherishes the longstanding friendship with China, firmly upholds the one-China principle, and looks forward to taking the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further deepen and advance bilateral relations, he said.
On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang also exchanged congratulations with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape.
China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and advance the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea, Li said in the message.
For his part, Marape said that the Papua New Guinean government highly appreciates China's significant contributions to the country's economic and social development.
Papua New Guinea will continue to uphold the one-China principle it has long adhered to, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation with China across various fields and advance the development of the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries, said Marape.

item.title: Shanghai wins 1st WIPO City of Innovation award
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
WIPO Director General Daren Tang (L) presents an award to Chinese city Shanghai during the Inaugural Award Ceremony for the first WIPO City of Innovation award at the headquarters of the WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, Oct. 12, 2026. Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. (Xinhua/Lian Yi)
GENEVA, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award.
Launched for the first time in 2026, the WIPO City of Innovation award is open to cities across all 194 WIPO member states and is bestowed on visionary cities for their bold pledges to foster innovation and creativity over the coming year. The three winners were chosen from 15 finalist cities.
According to WIPO, Shanghai's vision is to strengthen its position as an international hub for science, technology and intellectual property (IP), while fostering a broader culture of innovation and creativity. Its pledges include expanding IP education and services, opening innovation infrastructure and data, supporting cultural and creative industries, and strengthening connections between research, industry, entrepreneurs and investors.
Zhou Yaming, Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, said the award represents WIPO's strong recognition of Shanghai's innovative developments and its efforts in building a thriving IP ecosystem.
"It also reflects the international community's endorsement of China's commitment to open innovation, mutual benefits and shared success," He said.
Winners were selected by an independent international jury of high-profile experts in the cultural and creative sectors, urban planning, community development, and innovation-driven growth.
Andrea Dempster Chung, member of the International Jury Panel and Co-Founder & Executive Director for Kingston Creative, said Shanghai's application was extremely impressive, not just because of its strong research and development base that the city already had, but for the sheer scale of its ambitions and the strength of pledges.
"This would be pivotal in shifting the city's future and this is one of the reasons why Shanghai was selected," she said.
People attend the Inaugural Award Ceremony for the first WIPO City of Innovation award at the headquarters of the WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, Oct. 12, 2026. Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. (Xinhua/Lian Yi)

item.title: China to cut NEV export tax rebate for high-quality auto industry growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
An aerial drone photo taken on April 10, 2026 shows vehicles to be exported at a ro-ro dock of Tianjin Port in north China's Tianjin. (Photo by Du Penghui/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- China announced on Monday that it will cut the value-added tax (VAT) export rebate rate for new energy vehicles (NEVs) to 9 percent from 13 percent starting April 1, 2027.
VAT export rebates for e-cigarette devices and related products will be scrapped from the same date, according to a statement jointly issued by the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration.
Export consumption tax policies for products subject to the tax will remain unchanged, with existing tax refund or exemption arrangements continuing to apply, the statement said.
The adjustment comes as China has continued to optimize export tax rebate policies.
The country scrapped VAT export rebates for photovoltaic products from April 1, 2026, while cutting the rebate rate for battery products to 6 percent from 9 percent on the same date. The rebates for battery products will be eliminated from Jan. 1, 2027.
China is the world's largest market for NEVs, a category that includes battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles. The sector has expanded rapidly in recent years, with automakers increasingly looking to overseas markets for growth.
Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities, told business news network Yicai that cutting export tax rebates can, to some extent, reduce rat race competition and encourage companies to shift from low-price competition to technology and brand-based competition.
"China's NEVs are highly competitive internationally. Against the backdrop of tight global supplies of traditional energy, NEVs have met the needs of residents in Europe and the United States. Even with a partial rebate cut, they can retain sufficient competitiveness," Luo said. "Objectively, this also plays a positive role in stabilizing the macro tax burden and can better support the development of domestic demand."
During the January-September period, China's auto exports totaled 8.205 million units, including over 4 million NEVs, more than double the level a year earlier, according to the latest data.
"Despite a complex and severe external environment, exports have continued to grow rapidly, demonstrating strong resilience, while domestic new growth drivers are being steadily unleashed and the share of NEV sales is rising steadily," said Chen Shihua, deputy secretary-general of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers.
Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, the industry is expected to maintain steady operation, Chen said.

item.title: Zheng Qinwen claims maiden WTA 1000 title at China Open
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Zheng Qinwen poses with the trophy during the awarding ceremony after the women's singles final between Zheng Qinwen of China and Mirra Andreeva of Russia at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Sun Fei)
BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen captured the women's singles title at the 2026 China Open on Sunday, defeating fourth-seeded Russian Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in the final to claim her maiden WTA 1000 crown before breaking down in tears during an emotional celebration on home soil.
"The feeling is incredible. Winning here in Beijing, in front of my home crowd, has always been one of my dreams," Zheng said after the match.
The victory also made Zheng the first Chinese player to win the singles title at the China Open.
"Today's match was extremely tough. Mirra is a great player, and she broke my serve right at the start," Zheng said. "I just had to take it one point at a time and keep telling myself to hang in there and never give up. After playing so many matches, I was physically and mentally exhausted. But playing in front of my home crowd gave me that extra strength to keep pushing through."
"I want to congratulate Mirra on her outstanding achievement at Roland Garros this year. I never had a chance to congratulate you in person, so I want to do that now. Congratulations on reaching the final this week as well. You are such a young and talented player, and congratulations to you and your team on everything you've achieved," she added.
Since winning Olympic gold at the Paris 2024 Games, a persistent right elbow injury has disrupted Zheng's career and required surgery in July 2025. Her ranking subsequently fell from a career-high No. 4 in 2024 to as low as No. 160 in mid-June 2026.
"I want to thank my team for supporting me throughout this journey. I've been through a very tough year, and I couldn't have done this without you. Last but not least, I want to thank all the sponsors, the referees, and all the staff who have worked so hard throughout the week. And thank you to all the fans for your incredible support. This title belongs to all of you, too!"
The victory earned Zheng 1,000 ranking points and 1,151,380 U.S. dollars in prize money, lifting her to No. 23 in the live WTA rankings.
Zheng Qinwen (5th R, front) poses with the ballboys and ballgirls during the awarding ceremony after the women's singles final between Zheng Qinwen of China and Mirra Andreeva of Russia at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Sun Fei)
Zheng Qinwen (R) and Mirra Andreeva pose with their trophies during the awarding ceremony after the women's singles final between Zheng Qinwen of China and Mirra Andreeva of Russia at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Sun Fei)

item.title: Long March legacy inspires innovation breakthroughs in city of historic turning point
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
*The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. The spirit of what American journalist Edgar Snow described as "an odyssey unequaled in modern times" continues to inspire China as it pursues its Second Centenary Goal.
*The Long March in Guizhou was about breaking through encirclement and relying on one's own strength. Today, we are far removed from the smoke of war, but in science and technology, we are also making breakthroughs.
*China's 15th Five-Year Plan, released in the first half of this year, sets out comprehensive arrangements for accelerating high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology and fostering new quality productive forces.
People visit the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Aug. 17, 2026. (Photo by Zhang Zhengju/Xinhua)
ZUNYI, Guizhou, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Lei Guangren has crossed the weathered stone arch bridge countless times in Zunyi, a city in southwest China's Guizhou Province. Known as Yinghong Bridge, or "Welcoming the Red Army Bridge," it bears quiet witness to the Chinese Red Army's epic Long March more than nine decades ago.
Such Long March-associated place names pepper every corner of the mountainous city, earning Zunyi its resonant title: the "city of historic turning point."
"The Zunyi Meeting, held here during the Long March, marked a life-or-death turning point in the history of the Communist Party of China (CPC)," said Lei, 78, former curator of the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum. "From then on, the Party found the right direction and leadership, stayed the course toward its goals, defeated the enemies and embarked on a path of independence and self-reliance."
The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Lei believes the spirit of what American journalist Edgar Snow described as "an odyssey unequaled in modern times" continues to inspire China as it pursues its Second Centenary Goal.
In October 1934, the CPC was forced to retreat from the Central Soviet Area in east China's Jiangxi Province and move northwest after enduring a series of encirclement campaigns by rival forces of the Kuomintang party (KMT). The CPC-led Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the KMT troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle.
In downtown Zunyi stands a two-story gray-and-white building where Lei had worked for a decade. In January 1935, at a critical historical crossroads, the Zunyi Meeting was held in this building, establishing Mao Zedong's leading position in the CPC Central Committee and the Red Army in practice. The spirit of the Zunyi Meeting -- characterized by firm conviction, commitment to truth, independence and self-reliance, and unity -- continues to resonate today.
In his book "The Long March: The Untold Story," American journalist and author Harrison Salisbury wrote that China's course "had been set for at least half a century to come."
Tourists visit the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Tian Jinhong/Xinhua)
The Red Army subsequently won its first major victory since the start of the Long March at Loushan Pass in northern Zunyi and later broke out of enemy encirclement through its four crossings of the Chishui River.
"My mother told me that she was working when Red Army soldiers passed by our home. They borrowed a douqiang to shelter from the rain," Lei recalled.
A douqiang is a bamboo-woven tool traditionally used in southern China for drying grain. By the time the rain stopped, the soldiers had already reached the neighboring village. Before leaving, however, they asked local residents to make sure the tool was returned to Lei's mother.
Salisbury's book also mentions Kong Xianquan, a Red Army soldier who led troops in an assault during the Battle of Loushan Pass. Hit by six bullets in the hip, Kong was left behind in Guizhou to recover from his wounds. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, he helped establish the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum and became its first curator.
Today, his granddaughter Kong Xia has spent more than three decades sharing stories of China's revolutionary history.
"In Zunyi, stories of the Red Army are passed down like family heirlooms, reminding each new generation not to forget where we came from or where we are going," she said.
For 56-year-old Kong, Zunyi is a city where tradition and modernity coexist. Xiaolongshan, where some Red Army martyrs were buried, was renamed Hongjunshan, or Red Army Mountain. Year after year, visitors come to pay tribute here beside a bronze statue of a Red Army soldier draped in red silk by local residents.
Beyond these landmarks, a 10-minute walk from the site of the Zunyi Meeting stands the theater for "The Great Turning Point," a large-scale immersive production about the Long March, where history is retold through live performance.
Chen Jinghong, a visitor from southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, brought her 10-year-old daughter to see the show. "It is like planting a seed in a child's heart, allowing her to experience the culture of the Long March and gradually understand and appreciate it as she grows up," Chen said.
But Zunyi is far more than a museum of revolution. It has undergone dramatic transformation. When the Red Army passed through, its population stood at just over 30,000. By 2025, the permanent population of its central urban area exceeded 1.6 million, with an urbanization rate of 61 percent.
An aerial drone photo taken on July 31, 2026 shows the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua)
And it is not just Zunyi that has developed. Guizhou, a mountainous province with no natural plains, has emerged as a "museum of bridges." Nearly half of the world's tallest bridges stand here.
"The Long March in Guizhou was about breaking through encirclement and relying on one's own strength," Kong said. "Today, we are far removed from the smoke of war, but in science and technology, we are also making breakthroughs."
One striking example is the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in Guizhou. Holding world records both as the highest and the longest-span steel truss girder suspension bridge located in mountainous terrain, it has been dubbed by Chinese internet users a bridge that is "world No. 1, both horizontally and vertically."
Its main cables and upper structural components were produced by Guizhou Wire Rope Co., Ltd. The core steel wires were both developed and manufactured in Guizhou, forming a critical lifeline for the project.
"Wire-rope production used to be dominated in many areas by European and American companies. After the efforts of several generations, our products are now widely used in major equipment across land, sea and air, helping overcome technological bottlenecks," said Yang Zhengyan, director of a product research and development office at Guizhou Wire Rope.
At Laoyashan, where fierce fighting involving the Red Army once took place, bullet marks can still be seen on the rocks. At the foot of the mountain lies the old factory compound of Guizhou Wire Rope.
It was there that Yang and his team conducted countless tests to develop a mooring cable for offshore engineering.
Such cables had previously been expensive and required long procurement cycles, posing constraints on the development of China's offshore oil and gas resources.
"There is no room for failure with a product like this, so for many tests that would normally have been conducted only once, we ran them over and over again. We also pioneered some testing methods," Yang said.
In August 2023, the first permanent mooring cable for a floating production, storage and offloading unit, or FPSO, developed by Guizhou Wire Rope, was successfully deployed in the mooring system of the "Nanhai Fenjin" FPSO. It marked China's first application of a domestically produced permanent mooring cable for an FPSO, ending the country's long-standing reliance on foreign products in this field.
The group is now capable of mass-producing the cable. It can be used not only for deep-sea oil production platforms, but also for offshore wind power platforms. The system can reduce the sea area occupied by conventional mooring systems to about one-tenth, while also reducing their environmental footprint.
"The spirit of the Long March tells me to find the right direction, not to act blindly, and not to fear hardship or failure," said Yang, a 46-year-old Guizhou native.
This photo taken on Aug. 17, 2026 shows a view of Loushan Pass in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Shi Qiangui)
For another Zunyi native, 52-year-old Lin Guojun, chairman of Shenzhen Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd., the city has also played an important role in his company's growth.
Busbar holds more than 580 patents and international certifications, with its products used in new energy vehicles, wind power, solar power, smart grids and other new energy industries.
"We began developing our new energy business in 2008. It was an attempt to overtake on a curve," Lin recalled. "Back then, we had neither a market nor the technology, and the world did not believe China could develop a new energy industry."
In 2012, when the company encountered difficulties and struggled to fulfill orders, Lin turned his attention to Zunyi.
"Some of our equipment would shut down when temperatures became too high. Zunyi has a favorable natural environment, supporting industries, access to many major surrounding cities, and supportive policies," said Liu Yong, production and operations manager of Zunyi Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd.
A new factory was completed in just seven months. Inside the plant, many production processes are semi-automated, with more than 40 robots and robotic arms operating in an orderly fashion to ensure greater consistency in product quality.
The Zunyi facility now focuses on developing and manufacturing high-voltage system components for new energy vehicles, including charging connectors, charging piles, high-voltage relays and high-voltage wiring harnesses. Its products are supplied directly to domestic and overseas automakers.
Lin, who grew up listening to stories about the Red Army, said he sees parallels between the Long March and his own industry.
"From a time when China's new energy sector was little known globally to today, when Chinese new energy vehicles have won worldwide recognition, our work in this industry has itself been a breakthrough," he said. "It takes perseverance and conviction to see something like this through."
Tourists experience VR devices at the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Yuan Fuhong/Xinhua)
China's 15th Five-Year Plan, released in the first half of this year, sets out comprehensive arrangements for accelerating high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology and fostering new quality productive forces. Among its seven major economic and social development goals for 2026-2030 is substantially boosting the country's capacity for independent innovation.
Zunyi's government work report this year also called for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system.
The national vision also plays out in ordinary people's lives. Kong is thinking of replacing her family's gasoline car with a new energy vehicle. A frequent traveler across China, she recently took a high-speed train to Yan'an. The trip, which once took the Red Army nine months, now takes less than nine hours.
Her 27-year-old son Jiang Xiao carries the legacy forward as part of a youth lecture group, sharing stories of the Long March.
"Every generation has different experiences and its own interpretation of the Long March spirit," Kong said. "Yet the spirit never fades with time, and these stories deserve to be passed on."

item.title: Flag-raising ceremony held at Tian'anmen Square to celebrate 77th founding anniversary of PRC
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
A flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China (PRC) was held at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing on Thursday.
The Guard of Honor of the Chinese People's Liberation Army escorted the national flag to the square, while the military band played the national anthem.
Many people from across China gathered at the square to watch the ceremony.

item.title: Activities held across China to celebrate National Day
item.description:

Cities across China are decorating landmark sites with national flags and floral displays as National Day arrives, and people hold various activities to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
